Runtime package for the Minecraft Bedrock Inventory Editor.

## What changed in v0.5.30

- **No native database engine:** the editor reads and writes Bedrock worlds with its own Python code. Setup installs only hash-checked prebuilt packages for Python 3.12–3.14; Microsoft C++ Build Tools, the Windows SDK and the Visual C++ Redistributable are not needed, and the runtime ZIP contains no LevelDB wheels. A save adds a new write-ahead log to the world's database and leaves the existing database files unchanged; Minecraft integrates that log the next time it opens the world. Amulet-LevelDB is used only as an independent reference in the tests, so its license terms do not apply to the runtime.
- **Clear refusals:** the editor names the reason when it refuses a save because Minecraft, a Bedrock server or another editor instance has the world open, or because the world was not closed cleanly. Loading the world once in Minecraft or on the server and closing it normally resolves the second case. On Linux, a running Bedrock server holds no database lock; there the server-status check is the protection.
- **Unknown save outcome:** if a save fails after data may already have reached the disk, the editor reports that the outcome is unknown, keeps the backup and blocks further saves until the world is reloaded. Errors that occur before anything is written remain ordinary errors that can be retried.
- **Faster reload after saving:** after an ordinary save of one existing player, the editor keeps the world's player list instead of scanning the whole world again. On large worlds, reloading after a save takes well under a second instead of many seconds.
- **Walking speed that takes effect:** the previous walking speed field edited `walkSpeed` in the player's abilities. In Bedrock that value only sets the field of view: a higher value zoomed the view, but the player did not walk faster. The new **Walking speed** field edits the `minecraft:movement` attribute, which Bedrock uses for the actual speed; sprinting still adds to it. It also sets `walkSpeed` to the same value, so the field of view stays normal. `walkSpeed` remains available as **Walking field of view**, with a note on what it does. The walking speed is read-only while the attribute is missing, carries modifiers (for example from sprinting or an effect at the moment the world was saved) or has an unexpected structure; the reason is shown below the fields.
- **Vertical flying speed:** a new field edits `verticalFlySpeed` (0–20, vanilla 1), the speed of climbing and descending while flying. The flying speed field (`flySpeed`) is labelled as horizontal flight. Player migration copies `verticalFlySpeed` together with the other speeds.
- **Checkboxes without effect are gone:** Minecraft recalculates flying, floating, invulnerability, instant block breaking and build permission from the game mode and the player permission level when a player loads, so edits to these checkboxes were lost in the game. The "Place blocks" checkbox also wrote the Java tag name `mayBuild`, which Bedrock ignores and removes on its next save. The editor no longer shows or writes these values; change them through the game mode and player permissions in Minecraft. Values already stored in a world stay untouched.
- **Shorter slot details:** the NBT details of a slot no longer contain the "Show detail log" section, which repeated the table and the expert NBT shown above it. **Copy details** still copies the complete text, including player and world path.
- **Safer backup restore:** restore writes every extracted file and folder to disk before it replaces the current world. If that fails, the restore stops while the current world is still in place, and the safety backup is kept.
- **Clearer error for oversized requests:** a request whose JSON is nested deeper than the decoder allows gets the same "invalid request" error as other malformed JSON instead of a server error.

Validation includes the complete Python suite, the browser tests, comparisons of the new write path with the native LevelDB engine (identical log bytes, randomized alternating sessions, interrupted writes and locking) on synthetic data and on copies of real worlds, Bedrock Dedicated Server 1.26.51.1 engine checks, restore tests in which writing files or folders to disk fails, byte-for-byte comparisons of the new speed writes against an independent NBT implementation, and in-game checks with the Minecraft client 1.26.52 on Windows: inventory, Ender Chest, effects, a new horse and backup restore through the new write path; walking speed with and without sprinting, horizontal and vertical flying speed, and flying, instant block breaking and build permission following the game mode. See the [save contract](https://github.com/dadeeen/MCBE_Inventory_Editor/blob/v0.5.30/docs/save_contract.md) for validation boundaries.

This release removes Amulet-LevelDB from the runtime and adds no dependencies. Python 3.12–3.14 remain supported. Existing installations start without running `setup.bat` again; an Amulet-LevelDB package left in an existing `.venv` is not used. **If upgrading from v0.5.21 or earlier:** run `setup.bat` once before `start.bat` to install the Waitress server the editor uses since v0.5.22. When skipping several versions, the notes of the skipped [releases](https://github.com/dadeeen/MCBE_Inventory_Editor/releases) describe their changes.

> **Before every edit:** stop Minecraft or the Bedrock server and create a complete, independent copy of the world. Keep that copy until the edited world has been verified in Minecraft. App-created backups are an additional safeguard, not a replacement.

Download the asset ending in `_runtime.zip` together with its `.sha256` file. The automatically generated **Source code** archives are repository snapshots, not ready-to-run packages.

- Installation, Docker and LAN setup: [README](https://github.com/dadeeen/MCBE_Inventory_Editor/blob/main/README.md) · [Deutsch](https://github.com/dadeeen/MCBE_Inventory_Editor/blob/main/README.de.md)
- Supported security boundary and vulnerability reporting: [SECURITY](https://github.com/dadeeen/MCBE_Inventory_Editor/blob/main/SECURITY.md) · [Deutsch](https://github.com/dadeeen/MCBE_Inventory_Editor/blob/main/SECURITY.de.md)

Docker images are published to `ghcr.io/dadeeen/mcbe-inventory-editor`. Prefer the exact version tag for deployments; `latest` and minor tags are intentionally mutable.
